paper_title: Towards Predicting Any Human Trajectory In Context
caption: Performance change brought by different sizes of the in-context pool.
model_annotation: This line chart illustrates how the minimum ADE₂₀ metric changes across different ratios of an in-context pool, comparing five methods: TrajICL, Head Tuning, FT, LoRA 16, and LoRA 64. The x-axis represents the “Ratio,” ranging from 0.0 to 1.0 in increments of 0.2, marked numerically along the axis. The y-axis represents “minADE₂₀ (←),” scaled linearly from 15.5 to 17.5, with tick marks at regular intervals of 0.5. The blue line, representing TrajICL, starts at approximately 16.7 and decreases monotonically to 15.5. The orange line, representing Head Tuning, begins at approximately 17.5 and declines slightly to around 17.2. The green line, representing FT, starts at 17.0, dips to 16.9, rises slightly to 16.95, then falls to 15.9 before rising again to 16.0. The red line, representing LoRA 16, begins at approximately 17.4 and decreases steadily to 16.9. The purple line, representing LoRA 64, starts at approximately 17.4 and declines gradually to 16.8.

model_annotations.English: This line plot illustrates how the minimum average displacement error (minADE₂₀, in meters) changes across different ratios of the in-context pool size, comparing five different fine-tuning methods: TrajICL (blue line with circle markers), Head Tuning (orange line with circle markers), FT (green line with circle markers), LoRA 16 (red line with circle markers), and LoRA 64 (purple line with circle markers). The x-axis, labeled "Ratio," is a linear scale ranging from 0 to 1.0, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. The y-axis, labeled "minADE₂₀ (m)", is also linear and ranges from 15.5 to 17.5. The TrajICL line starts at approximately 16.7 m and steadily decreases to 15.5 m. The Head Tuning line begins at approximately 17.5 m and declines slightly to about 17.2 m. The FT line starts at 17.0 m, dips to 16.0 m, and then rises slightly to 16.1 m. The LoRA 16 line begins at 17.4 m and decreases to 16.9 m. The LoRA 64 line starts at 17.4 m, dips to 17.0 m, and then declines to 16.8 m.
